acts: Take one idea you dropped last year one step further.
Tell one person about a plan you have kept quiet.
Add ten minutes to the same project every day for a month.
Bring one piece to its end before you begin the next.
Drop one plan this month for good.
Tell three people about the venture you have in mind.
Ask once for the price you think your work is worth.
Put the idea in front of a real buyer this month.
Take one slow weekend.
Let the numbers wait.
Put yourself under one.
Sign up for the race, the exam or the course with a date on it.
Hold one fixed hour each week for it and do not move it.
Cut one task this week that nobody asked you for.
Ask what is needed, then do that much and stop.
Pick one hard question and collect three answers before you decide.
Sort what you hear into what you will use and what you will drop.
Clear one hour a week for a subject outside your field.
Ship one piece as a draft.
Share one rough idea with a group this week.
Every push you make draws on a reserve that was small to begin with.
Rest a full day after any big push.
Ask a friend for the whole answer rather than guessing it.
Hand half of one shared task to a peer.
Finish one job you have put off before Sunday.
Keep the same day each week for one steady task.
